input:

There is no way I can write this review without giving Russell, the owner of Body Cycle, a shout out. Russell's passion for fitness and cycling is so evident, as is his desire for all of his clients to succeed. He is always dropping in to classes to check in/provide encouragement, and is open to ideas and recommendations from anyone. Russell always wears a smile on his face, even when he's kicking your butt in class!
Improve this in GPT way:
After years of taking spin classes, I can confidently say that Body Cycle stands in a league of its own. The studio is immaculate, the bikes are superb, and the instructors are both welcoming and incredibly motivating, ensuring every session is a first-rate workout.

For those with busy schedules, the seamless online booking system is a game-changer—it simplifies planning and eliminates the need for long sign-up queues common elsewhere.

This review would be incomplete without highlighting Russell, the owner. His genuine passion for fitness and cycling is palpable, matched by a sincere commitment to every client’s success. He frequently visits classes to offer encouragement, actively welcomes feedback, and consistently leads with a positive attitude—even while pushing you to your limits.

input: Loved this tour! I grabbed a groupon and the price was great. This tour was one of my favorite parts of my trip!
Improve this in GPT way: This tour was a highlight of my New Orleans visit! As a first-time visitor with little historical knowledge, it was the perfect introduction. The meeting point is in front of a grocery store—convenient for grabbing water—and includes a restroom stop at a visitor center. Highly recommended for an engaging and well-paced overview of the city!

input:
My experience with Shalimar was nothing but wonderful. 
I wanted to get my engagement ring sized and was told over the phone that it could probably be done within the day. 
When I brought it by, the team confirmed that the jeweler would be able to accommodate my same-day request and that it would be around $40 (simple band, decrease by three full sizes).
I checked my size one more time, confirmed, and left to let them do their thing.
When I came to pick up later that afternoon, the ring was too small. It's very important to note that Shalimar sized the ring perfectly, but that I made a mistake and should've gone up a half-size.
The Shalimar group were completely understanding and accommodating, even resizing my ring back up and getting it back to me within an hour at no charge! Even though it was my mistake!
The associates' attitudes in dealing with what was a pretty embarrassing situation instantly earned my satisfaction and loyalty as a customer. Very grateful for such a wonderful experience.
Improve this in GPT way:
My experience with Shalimar was truly exceptional. I needed my engagement ring resized and was informed by phone that same-day service was likely. Upon arrival, the team confirmed the jeweler could accommodate the request, estimating a cost of around $40 for reducing the simple band by three sizes. After double-checking my size, I left the ring with them.

Upon pickup that afternoon, I discovered the ring was too small. Crucially, the error was mine—Shalimar had sized it perfectly to my initial instruction, but I realized I needed an additional half-size. Despite this being my mistake, the team was completely understanding. They promptly resized the ring upward and had it ready for me within an hour, refusing to charge for the additional work.

The associates’ gracious and accommodating attitude in an admittedly embarrassing situation instantly secured my satisfaction and loyalty. I am deeply grateful for such a wonderful and patient customer service experience.

input:
The bun makes the Sonoran Dog. It's like a snuggie for the pup. A first, it seems ridiculous and almost like it's going to be too much, exactly like everyone's favorite blanket with sleeves. Too much softness, too much smush, too indulgent.  Wrong. It's warm, soft, chewy, fragrant, and it succeeds where other famed Sonoran Dogs fail. 

The hot dog itself is flavorful, but I would prefer that it or the bacon have a little more bite or snap to better hold their own against the dominant mustard and onions. 

I'm with the masses on the carne asada caramelo. Excellent tortilla, salty, melty cheese, and great carne. 

Super cheap and you can drive through.
Improve this in GPT way:
The bun is essential to the Sonoran Dog, acting like a snug, edible blanket. At first, its soft, pillowy excess seems almost ridiculous—too much indulgence. Yet it works, providing a warm, fragrant, and perfectly chewy foundation that outshines other versions.

While the hot dog is flavorful, I wish it or the bacon had more snap to stand up to the bold mustard and onions.

As for the carne asada caramelo, I agree with the popular praise: excellent tortilla, salty melted cheese, and superb meat.

It’s all super affordable and conveniently drive-through ready.

input: Upland is a brewery based out of Bloomington, Indiana that has become popular enough to open up a couple additional locations in central Indiana. My opinion is that Upland's pizza might serve as a nice appetizer for a group, but I'll be sticking with their burgers or tenderloins as my meal of choice on future visits.
Improve this in GPT way: Based in Bloomington, Indiana, Upland Brewery has expanded with several locations across central Indiana, thanks to its well-earned popularity. The margherita pizza I tried featured a very thin, cracker-like crust and was overall quite light. However, on future visits, I’ll remain loyal to their burgers or tenderloins as my primary choice.

input:
I was really between 3 and 4 stars for this one. I LOVE the 96th street Naked Tchopstix so I was very excited to see this one which is closer to my house.
The vibe is totally different as this is geared more to take out although they do have a decent size dining area. You order at the counter and they deliver it.
My daughter and I tried the sushi bowl. You pick up a piece of paper and  select from a choice of proteins, vegetables, rice and toppings. I like the fact that it is on paper and you don't have to guess what things are or have to shout over the counter to tell the server what you want. The sushi bowl was good but not wonderful. The choices particularly of the vegetables seemed a little too limiting and I felt I had more rice than other food items. The sauces were tasty. My husband ordered the Maui roll which is my favorite roll at the 96th street location and this just was not up that standard. It was good but the quality and consistently was not as good as at 96th street. I would go back though and I think a lot of people would be happy with the sushi bowls. I do want to make a comment about the low reviews that people have given the place because of service. People - it is a sushi place - it isn't McDonalds- so it will be a bit slower. You are not going to order and get out of there in five minutes even though it is called express. As a healthy alternative to fast food in the area, it is worth the wait. Oh and try the bubble tea. I had the strawberry and it was quite yummy. Next time I am going to try the vanilla chai.
Improve this in GPT way:
I was genuinely torn between a three and four-star rating for this location. As a devoted fan of the 96th Street Naked Tchopstix, I was thrilled to find a branch closer to my home.

The atmosphere here is distinctly different, oriented more toward takeout, though they do offer a reasonably sized dining area. Service operates counter-style: you place your order and it’s brought to your table. My daughter and I opted for the sushi bowl, which involves selecting your ingredients—protein, vegetables, rice, and toppings—on a paper checklist. I appreciated this system; it eliminates guesswork and the need to raise your voice across the counter.

The sushi bowl was good, though not exceptional. I found the vegetable choices somewhat limited, and the ratio felt heavy on rice compared to other components. That said, the sauces were quite flavorful. My husband ordered the Maui roll, a favorite of mine at the 96th Street restaurant, but here it didn’t quite meet the same standard. It was still enjoyable, yet the quality and consistency fell short of the original.

I would return, especially for the sushi bowls, which I believe many would find satisfying. I also feel compelled to address some critical reviews regarding service speed. Patrons should remember this is a sushi spot, not fast food—even with “express” in the name, don’t expect to be in and out in five minutes. As a healthier alternative in the area, it’s worth a little patience.

On a final note, don’t miss the bubble tea. The strawberry flavor I tried was delicious, and I look forward to sampling the vanilla chai next time.

input: We checked in around 2:30 pm.  Check-in was quick and easy with complimentary valet parking (always appreciated).  The Peppermill is huge and reminded us of the Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.  They have around eight restaurants on site offering almost any type of food you could want.  The casino area is huge, rivaling almost anything you could find in Las Vegas.  One thing we noticed is that many of the slot machines were noted as being penny machines, but when you actually started to play them you realized they had minimum bets of anywhere from 30 cents to $5.  Talk about false advertising!  We were in the Tuscany Tower on the 12th floor.  Our room had a nice view of the huge pool area.  Our room was large and featured free WiFi (likewise always appreciated), a huge bathroom area with large shower (with two shower heads), TV, a large jetted bathtub and a phone next to the commode.  There were dual sinks and lots of counter space.  Plenty of towels were supplied.  The roomy main area had a king bed with night stands, closet, TV, mini fridge, dresser with two drawers, a safe, table for computer or writing, complimentary bottles of water, and three nicely upholstered chairs and table.  The thermostat did a good job controlling the temperature and keeping it comfortable.  Staff were all courteous and helpful.  A very nice place and we enjoyed our stay.
Improve this in GPT way:
Our arrival at 2:30 pm was met with a swift and seamless check-in process, complemented by the welcome convenience of complimentary valet parking. The sheer scale of The Peppermill immediately evoked comparisons to Caesars Palace in Las Vegas. The property boasts an impressive array of approximately eight on-site restaurants, catering to nearly every culinary preference, alongside a vast casino floor that genuinely rivals its famed Nevada counterparts. A notable observation, however, was that many slots advertised as "penny machines" actually required minimum bets ranging from 30 cents to $5—a somewhat misleading practice.

We were situated in the Tuscany Tower on the 12th floor, where our spacious room offered a pleasant overlook of the expansive pool area. Amenities included reliable free WiFi, a generously sized bathroom with dual sinks, ample counter space, a large shower featuring two showerheads, and a jetted bathtub. The well-appointed main area contained a king bed, multiple seating options with three upholstered chairs, two televisions, a mini fridge, a work table, a safe, and complimentary bottled water. Climate control via the thermostat proved effective in maintaining consistent comfort throughout our visit.

Every member of the staff we encountered was consistently courteous and helpful. Overall, our experience was thoroughly enjoyable, solidifying The Peppermill as a highly commendable destination.

The good: price, location, dessert (edible food items are: baked chicken, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, Salad bar lol, meat and cheese bar, ravioli, pizza) also our waitress was bomb af

The meh: behind counter meat slicing station, shrimp (not even deveined), Mexican station

The bad: breakfast -worst eggs ever, actually worst, eggs. Le Benedict can't even cut through ham or English muffin (tried on all 3 occasions), steak, shrimp again, hell breaded items can't even, don't even. Decor it's the 1970 nightmare you can imagine

Tried 3 times and failed
Improve this in GPT way:
This place is cheap, and it tastes and feels exactly that way.

**The good:** The price, location, and desserts. Edible items include baked chicken, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, the salad bar, a meat and cheese station, ravioli, and pizza. Our waitress was also excellent.

**The meh:** The behind-counter meat slicing station, the shrimp (not even deveined), and the Mexican station.

**The bad:** Breakfast features the worst eggs imaginable. Eggs Benedict was inedible—the ham and English muffin were impossibly tough on all three visits. The steak, shrimp (again), and breaded items were also failures. The decor is a 1970s nightmare.

We gave it three chances, and it disappointed every time.

input:
The only reason I didn't give this restaurant a 5 star rating, is because of one single pretentious waiter. As a 4 night guest at Hotel Palomar, the location of the restaurant is an obvious plus. The first night of my stay, I met a coworker in the restaurant for a cocktail. When we arrived, the host staff were busy and not available, so we just walked in. The restaurant was not too busy, so we just looked at a small table next to the bar and proceeded to take a seat. A waiter came by and I quickly asked if we could have a seat, before sitting down and told him we'd only be having cocktails. He stumbled on his reply, and in an irritated/in-convinced tone, told me "I guess it would be fine" and basically just kept walking mid sentence. My guest and I brushed it off, and started having a conversation while looking at the drink menu. To make a long story short, he was distant and we both got the "couldn't be bothered" vibe from him. When it came to the bill, we asked if it could be split due to company transaction policies, and you would have thought asked him for some inconceivable task. We basically spent the rest of our night and elevator ride to our room in shock of the rudeness we had just experienced. 

Although that situation left a bad taste in our mouth, and the night before we decided to avoid the restaurant, we decided to grab another cocktail and give this place one more try. After looking around and ensuring "last nights waiter" wasn't on shift, we walked over to the bar and started looking over the menu. Instantly, the bartender greeted us with pleasant small talk and made us feel 100% welcome. He asked about our day, recommended cocktails and was a completely genuine person. This guy (I think his name was Ben) is an absolute star! He gave us lessons on Whiskey, described how to make classic cocktails, and was 100% invested in our experience. This is exactly what a bartender at a 4/5 star establishment should be - actually he exceeds that. He was kind, funny, friendly and completely redeemed this restaurant/bar from our terrible experience the night before. 
I also ordered room service last night from this restaurant, and it was amazing. The bacon wrapped dates and chocolate cake are to die for! Great restaurant and amazing bartender(s). Too bad one bad egg could have spoiled this experience.
Improve this in GPT way:
My sole reason for withholding a five-star rating is a single, pretentious waiter. As a guest at Hotel Palomar for four nights, the restaurant’s location was a clear convenience. On my first evening, I met a colleague there for a cocktail. The host stand was unattended, so we entered and, seeing the restaurant wasn’t crowded, approached a small table near the bar. Before sitting, I politely asked a passing waiter if we could take the seat, mentioning we only wanted drinks. He replied with an irritated, unconvinced, “I guess it would be fine,” then walked away mid-sentence. We dismissed his manner and began reviewing the drink menu. Throughout, he was distant, radiating a palpable “couldn’t be bothered” attitude. When we requested the bill be split for company expense purposes, he reacted as if we’d asked the impossible. My guest and I spent the rest of the evening, including the elevator ride to our room, stunned by such outright rudeness.

That encounter left a sour impression, and we initially avoided the restaurant the next night. Ultimately, we decided to give it another chance for a final cocktail. After confirming the previous night’s waiter wasn’t present, we approached the bar. Immediately, the bartender—I believe his name was Ben—greeted us with warm small talk, making us feel completely welcome. He asked about our day, offered excellent cocktail recommendations, and was utterly genuine. Ben was an absolute star: he gave us a mini-lesson on whiskey, explained how classic cocktails are crafted, and was fully invested in our experience. This is precisely what a bartender at a four- or five-star establishment should be—in fact, he exceeded that standard. His kindness, humor, and friendliness completely redeemed the restaurant and bar from our prior terrible experience.

I also ordered room service from the restaurant last night, and it was exceptional. The bacon-wrapped dates and the chocolate cake are to die for! This is a great restaurant with amazing bartenders. It’s just a shame that one bad egg nearly spoiled the entire experience.

input: Stopped by after a Sunday morning walk in the park - great food, coffee customer service - love the vibe in here
Improve this in GPT way: Stopping in after a Sunday park walk, I loved the excellent food, coffee, service, and the wonderful overall vibe.

input: In a word... "OVERRATED!".  The food took forever to come out.  The burger was WAY overcooked (Especially when I ordered it Medium Rare) and the Seafood Jumbalaya was Decent.  Not worth the price.  There are better places to eat in the french quarter.  It was not horrible, but for everything that we had heard about this place, I would have expected much better.
Improve this in GPT way: In a word: overrated. The service was slow, and my burger arrived well-done instead of medium-rare. The seafood jambalaya was merely decent. Given the price and its reputation in the French Quarter, I expected far better. While not terrible, there are superior dining options nearby. Overall, the experience failed to live up to the hype.

input: Comfortable bed, good breakfast, fast internet, great location, and low price. Overall I was really impressed with this place. However, if you stay on the top floors you may be waiting up to 15 minutes for an elevator in the morning.
Improve this in GPT way: This place impressed me with its comfortable bed, great breakfast, fast internet, prime location, and low price. The only drawback is that top-floor guests may face elevator waits of up to 15 minutes in the morning.

input: NEVER AGAIN. This is a so called restaurant that does nothing that a restaurant should other than prepare food, because the rest is done by the patron. Want water? Get up and go across the yard to get it. Want a drink, walk up a flight of stairs and pay cash. Want to sit in a dirty yard in dirty lawn chairs, enjoy yourself. The wait staff is mildy helpful in that they bring you your food after you go to the window and pay cash for it...kind of like New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood, but dirty and with live music (which is nice). It's a one in a lifetime experience for me...just once.
Improve this in GPT way: NEVER AGAIN. This establishment barely functions as a restaurant, outsourcing every duty beyond cooking to the customer. Patrons must fetch their own water from across the yard, climb stairs to purchase drinks with cash, and sit in a grimy outdoor space furnished with dirty lawn chairs. The staff’s sole contribution is delivering food after you pay cash at a window—reminiscent of a fast-food model, but notably dirtier. The live music was a pleasant touch, yet it couldn’t salvage the experience. For me, once was decidedly enough.

input:
If you want to pay for everything a la carte this is the place for you.  
Food wasn't terrible not impressive.
They brought a basket of chips and some tomato sauce which I asked politely for something spicier and some pico de gallo.  She brought them happily to me and the salsa was much better.  When asked what we would like to drink I asked for a coke and she brought out a bottle which I stated I wanted the fountain drink.  She said "oh that's only Pepsi".  Never mentioned that they only had bottle drinks for coke.  
We ordered our food which was reasonably priced, asked for sour cream and also to put cheese on the taco.  She let us know cheese was extra.  
It was $2.50 extra for another basket of chips.  
When I received the bill we paid more for the condiments then the actual food.  Side of sour cream 2.00, pico de gallo 2.50, salsa 2.00, chips 2.50, cheese 1.00 and the bottled coke that we didn't want 5.00.  
Just a suggestion...when you order anything make sure to ask if there is an extra charge.
Improve this in GPT way:
This establishment operates on a strictly à la carte basis, so be prepared to pay separately for each item. The food itself was acceptable, though not remarkable.

Service was pleasant—when I requested a spicier option and pico de gallo instead of the complimentary chips and tomato sauce, the server happily obliged. However, transparency around pricing was lacking. I ordered a Coke and was brought a bottle without being told fountain drinks weren’t available; only when I inquired did she mention they only serve Pepsi on tap. We added sour cream and cheese to a taco, learning only then that cheese cost extra. Another basket of chips was an additional $2.50.

The final bill revealed the issue: condiments and the unwanted bottled drink significantly outweighed the cost of the actual meals. Sour cream was $2.00, pico de gallo $2.50, salsa $2.00, chips $2.50, cheese $1.00, and the bottled Coke $5.00. My strong advice: always ask if there is an extra charge for *anything* you order.

input: The cafe was extremely cute. We came at 8am and they even had a jazz band playing at that time. I got the breakfast sandwich and it was delicious. I loved how they rolled the egg and put the bacon pieces inside. Great price for a filling breakfast!
Improve this in GPT way: This charming cafe surprised us with live jazz at 8 a.m. My breakfast sandwich was delicious, with the egg rolled neatly around pieces of bacon. It was a filling meal for a great price.

input:
On a scale of one to things that are awesome, this place is the bomb. 

I was drawn in by the promise of the duckfat frenchfries. Took the boy for his birthday and put our name in, had a drink around the corner while we waited and were given seats at the bar after about 45 minutes. 

We were waited on by Keith, the bartender, who was congenial, knowledgeable about his whiskeys and an all-around cool guy. We started with 3 cape may salts (two for me, one for the boy) and tater tots, both of which made me happy.

For dinner, I got Kentucky Fried Quail (stellar, though the succotash was not as exciting as I wanted it to be) and the boy got the 24$ Fois Gras burger, which was incredible. Worth every penny. The duckfat fries were pretty yummy, but not even the best part of the meal. I could've done without the cheese sauce, but as it was on the side I wasn't deterred.

I look forward to coming back here, with everyone I know.
Improve this in GPT way:
On a scale of ordinary to extraordinary, this restaurant is exceptional.

The initial draw was the renowned duck fat fries. To celebrate my son’s birthday, we added our name to the list and enjoyed a brief drink nearby. We were seated at the bar after approximately 45 minutes.

Our bartender, Keith, provided superb service—he was personable, deeply knowledgeable about whiskey, and thoroughly professional. We began with three Cape May Salts (two for me, one for my son) and an order of tater tots, both of which were delightful.

For our mains, I chose the Kentucky Fried Quail—stellar, though the accompanying succotash was somewhat underwhelming. My son had the $24 Foie Gras Burger, which was utterly incredible and worth every cent. The duck fat fries were delicious, yet not even the highlight of the meal. The optional cheese sauce was unnecessary, but easily omitted.

I eagerly anticipate returning and recommending this experience to everyone.

input: We started with the artichoke dip, big mistake. It was cold and the chips were stale. Mentioned to our waitress, but nothing came of it.  We ordered a large pizza, thin crust which after adding toppings it was a bit pricey for pizza.  Pizza was ok, not great. Except for not being our advocate our server was good.  I have been here before for Cardinals game, it was better then. Will try another venue next time.
Improve this in GPT way: We began with the artichoke dip—a regrettable choice. It was chilled, served with stale chips. Our complaint to the waitress went unaddressed. The thin-crust pizza, loaded with toppings, was overpriced and merely average. While our server was attentive, she didn’t advocate for us. Previous visits during Cardinals games were better, but next time we’ll dine elsewhere.

input: It was my fiance's birthday and he decided he wanted a good, laid back Thai restaurant for dinner. Yelp steered us in the Jasmine Rice direction, and it was definitely a good decision. We wanted the summer rolls, which were on the menu, but apparently will not be available until summer, so we settled on the pan-fried dumplings. The flavor was good, but I don't think we'd order them again. We got the green curry fried rice with duck and chicken pad thai. Both of those dishes were great, but the duck stole the show. That was some the of tastiest duck I've ever had. The pad thai was a bit sweet for us, so I think we'd try a different noodle dish when we return. But it was still very good, especially with some chili sauce mixed in. Our service was good, but other people had issues. One table was rushing to get to a show at the Kimmel Center and waited quite a while for their meal (and were going to be late). Another person who got take-out was missing one of their items (but the owner realized it and called him and walked the dish to his house, which was very nice). Overall, good quality Thai! We would definitely go back.
Improve this in GPT way:
For my fiancé’s birthday, he chose a relaxed Thai dinner, and Yelp led us to Jasmine Rice—a great recommendation. We initially wanted summer rolls, but learned they’re seasonal, so we opted for pan-fried dumplings instead. They were flavorful, though not something we’d reorder.  

For our mains, we selected the green curry fried rice with duck and the chicken pad thai. Both were excellent, but the duck truly stood out—some of the best I’ve ever tasted. The pad thai leaned sweet for our preference, so next time we’ll likely try a different noodle dish, though it was still delicious with a bit of chili sauce mixed in.  

Service was attentive for us, though we noticed some hiccups nearby. One table, hurrying to a show at the Kimmel Center, experienced a long wait that risked making them late. Another guest’s takeout order was missing an item, but the owner personally noticed, called, and even delivered it to their home—a very kind gesture.  

Overall, Jasmine Rice offers solid, quality Thai food. We’ll definitely return.

input: I absolutely love Courtney! She is hands down the best hairstylist I have ever had. The reason I think she is so great is that she knows what will look best on me and over the past year has understood my limits for styles. I always go into the salon and tell her to cut my hair how she thinks will look best, and I always leave blown away at what she does. You know you have a great stylist when you don't have to specify what you want done, but instead they see what needs to be done. Great stylist, great personality and very knowledgeable. I would highly recommend her to anyone who wants to look their best.
Improve this in GPT way: Courtney is simply the best hairstylist I’ve ever had. What makes her exceptional is her ability to discern what truly suits me, and over the past year she’s learned my style boundaries perfectly. I walk in, tell her to do what she thinks is best, and every time leave amazed by the results. A great stylist doesn’t need detailed instructions—they see what’s needed. With her talent, warm personality, and deep expertise, I highly recommend Courtney to anyone wanting to look their absolute best.

input:
I love the Brewpub for their variety of dishes.  Nachos, pizza and sandwiches.  Variety of beers to choose from crafted right on sight.  

Every time we go, the service is slow.  I think it's just the pace of the restaurant.  It's never a quick beer and a bite of food.  Instead, enjoy the patio and friends, savor that time.  

Kid and dog friendly environment.  Also great for your vegetarian and vegan friends.  

My go to is a half order of the nachos or fish & chips.  

Tried their Pumpkin Seasonal Beer and it's on par with some of my favorite pumpkins.
Improve this in GPT way: The Brewpub excels with its diverse menu, featuring nachos, pizza, sandwiches, and excellent vegetarian options. Their on-site crafted beers offer great variety, including a seasonal pumpkin ale that rivals my favorites. While service is leisurely—more suited for savoring time with friends on the patio than a quick bite—it complements the relaxed, kid and dog-friendly atmosphere. My personal standouts are the half-order of nachos and the fish & chips. It’s an ideal spot to unwind and enjoy good food and drink.

input: Farmhouse, rustic, chic.Helpful staff with great ideas to decorate your home. Prices reasonable. Store has items from Joanna Gaines ( Fixer Upper) and much more. Finally a good home store in SB with reasonable prices.
Improve this in GPT way: A rustic-chic farmhouse store with helpful staff and reasonable prices. Featuring Joanna Gaines’ Fixer Upper items and more, it’s a welcome home goods destination for Santa Barbara.

input: My brother came to visit and we wanted to pick up a six pack of good beers for a night in. Ended up staying and having a few while playing their Nintendo 64 (Super Smash Brothers, which the owner said was donated by fellow patrons). Improve this in GPT way: My brother visited, so we grabbed a six-pack for a night in. input:
My go to menu is coconut soup and pad thai with protein. I tried same menu here. 
Actually really like their coconut soup. They used enough amount of coconut milk that soup was really creamy and wasn't over powering with herb. I am so used to Americanized thai cuisine that I prefer less herb on my dish except cilantro.
Pat thai was great too. Liked the amount of peanut they used, noodle was chewy and perfect and not too sweet. They gave me generous amount of chicken and white meat wasn't dry so I was very happy with my meal.
Improve this in GPT way:
My usual order is coconut soup and pad thai with chicken. I tried both here and was impressed. The coconut soup was perfectly creamy, rich with coconut milk and not overpowered by herbs. As someone accustomed to Americanized Thai food, I prefer subtler herb flavors, so this suited me perfectly.

The pad thai was also excellent. It had a generous sprinkle of peanuts, the noodles were delightfully chewy, and the sauce wasn’t overly sweet. The chicken was plentiful and tender, making for a very satisfying meal.

input: Excellent service! Great diner food and breakfast is served all day. Came here for lunch- they were busy but very friendly and hospitable. Easy to get to off the 295.
Improve this in GPT way: Excellent service and friendly staff, even when busy. They serve great diner food and all-day breakfast, conveniently located off the 295.

input:

Their food is better than expected. I always get wings and fries. (be careful of the wtf sauce though) Sometimes it takes a real long time to get the bartenders attention, but the place is usually packed. And if you're lucky the always sunny crew will pop in!
Improve this in GPT way: My new Saturday night favorite! Though I was disappointed when Lucy’s closed, this bar right across the street is a welcome surprise. The food—especially the wings and fries—exceeds expectations (but beware the “WTF” sauce!). Service can be slow when it’s crowded, which is often. Still, the lively atmosphere is worth it, and you might even spot the *It’s Always Sunny* cast!

input:
We were a bit weary about trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf as more often than not, many places like these (see Cannery Row, Monterey) feast on a captive audience and provide sub-standard fare at high prices.

However, emboldened by the perennial good reviews on Yelp, we suppressed our initial observations and went ahead with the trying it out. The place is small, so definitely plan ahead. You will have to wait, so either you know, just do so, or perhaps try to visit outside of peak hours. Luckily, our wait was only about 20 minutes as the dinner rush was just leveling off.

The special was the local rock crab - $25 for 3 lbs of California Rock Crab, salad, and your choice of soup/chowder. After taking a look at a few trays of rock crab being served out, the wife and I both opted for it, as it looked awesome.  

The salad/chowder combo was great as you actually received hearty portions of each, so it was a good start. As much as I liked the chowder however, the Shrimp Bisque the wife ordered was amazing, so I would recommend that going forward. 

But enough of prattling on about side dishes: the rock crab tasted just as glorious as it looked. Juicy, buttery chunks of white crab meat await you, just a few cracks away. While the rock crab shells are pretty thick, once cracked, they splinter and separate easily, a good sign they are cooked to perfection. The rock crabs provided a great amount of meat for what I felt to be the least amount of work you're going to do for crab, King or otherwise. 

We were thoroughly satisfied with our meal and along with the special being an overall great value, devouring the Rock Crab at SBSC turned out to be one of the favorite meals on the trip. I think ordering crab here is a safe proposition indeed.
Improve this in GPT way:
We had our reservations about trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf. Places like this—think Cannery Row in Monterey—often rely on a captive audience, serving mediocre food at inflated prices. Yet, consistently strong Yelp reviews encouraged us to set aside our skepticism and give it a try.

The restaurant is quite small, so planning ahead is essential. Be prepared to wait, either patiently or by aiming for off-peak hours. Fortunately, our wait was only about twenty minutes, as the dinner crowd was beginning to thin.

That evening’s special was local rock crab: three pounds of California rock crab, a salad, and a choice of soup or chowder for twenty-five dollars. After seeing several impressive trays delivered to other tables, my wife and I both decided to order it.

The meal began well with generous portions of both salad and chowder. While the chowder was satisfying, my wife’s shrimp bisque was exceptional—a clear winner I’d recommend.

But the true star was the rock crab. It tasted every bit as magnificent as it looked: juicy, buttery chunks of white meat, just a few cracks away. Though the shells are thick, they split cleanly when cracked—a sure sign of perfect preparation. For the effort required, the yield of meat was impressive, rivaling even king crab in efficiency.

We left thoroughly satisfied. Between the exceptional flavor and the outstanding value, our rock crab feast at the Shellfish Company became one of the standout meals of our trip. Ordering crab here isn’t just a good choice—it’s a reliably excellent one.

input: I LOVE Weaver's Way and really disagree with some of the content in previous reviews. WW is not necessarily meant for convenience shopping. I am a single woman and I find that I have no trouble shopping at the co-op, during peak times or otherwise. I actually find the co-op to be a great place to shop if you live alone because I can get smaller quantities of items than if I shop at the corporate stores like Acme. I also enjoy the work hours - I've worked throughout the store, but most recently, I have been getting in my hours by participating in the membership committee. I wouldn't say that the community is necessarily made up of "tree huggers" and "earth children", though. The community is made up of a variety of similarly-minded folks from different backgrounds. I enjoy having a place to go to where I can obtain locally grown produce, a place that offers more natural, wholesome, and preservative-free foods than chain stores with prices way below that of Whole Foods. I enjoy interacting with other members and contributing to my local and global community. I don't find the membership fee or the work hours to be prohibitive being a single person vs. a family. I don't think that membership in a co-op is for everyone and, if you aren't single, it's definitely not a solo decision. If you're keen on being committed to the Weaver Way values, you couldn't find a better place to shop. If not, stick to the chain stores or just pay the 10% visitors' fee to pop in once in a while.
Improve this in GPT way:
I am a devoted fan of Weaver’s Way and feel compelled to offer a different perspective from some earlier reviews. It’s important to understand that the co-op isn’t designed primarily for convenience. As a single person, I shop there regularly—even during busy times—without issue. In fact, living alone makes it an ideal choice: I can purchase smaller, more manageable quantities than at large corporate grocers like Acme.

I also appreciate the member work requirement. I’ve fulfilled my hours in various roles and currently serve on the membership committee, which I find rewarding. While some may stereotype the community, it isn’t just “tree huggers” or “earth children.” It’s a diverse group of like-minded individuals from all walks of life.

What truly sets Weaver’s Way apart is its commitment to local, natural, and preservative-free foods—often at prices well below those of Whole Foods. I value accessing locally grown produce and knowing my spending supports both my local and global community. The membership fee and work hours are manageable even on a single income.

That said, a co-op isn’t for everyone. If you have a family, joining is a shared decision. But if you align with its values of community and sustainability, there’s no better place to shop. If not, chain stores remain an option, or you can always visit occasionally and pay the 10% non-member fee.

input: Honestly the food doesn't knock my socks off but other people seem to love this place. I go because my husband likes it as for me I'd rather go to a different BBQ spot. I guess it also depends on what you order.

input: I stopped here because it was by the hotel I was staying in. The guys working at the shop were super nice and friendly. I really like the buy one get one deal they do. Improve this in GPT way: I chose this spot due to its proximity to my hotel. The staff were exceptionally friendly, and I appreciated their buy-one-get-one offer. The hot wings were also quite good, generously coated in sauce—exactly how I like them. When I return to town, I’ll definitely be back for more pizza.

input: I've only had the cannolis here but they are awesome! They're freshly filled when ordered and the filling is phenomenal. Not too sweet, it's perfect. If you like cannoli, if you don't think you like cannoli, you should definitely get one from Termini Bros.
Improve this in GPT way: I’ve only tried the cannolis here, and they’re outstanding. Filled fresh to order, the filling is phenomenal—perfectly balanced, not too sweet. Whether you love cannoli or think you don’t, you must try one from Termini Bros.

input: Traveling through in our RV, stopped over in Granite City. Found this little gem of a cafe. Upon entering, the staff was very sweet and friendly. This is like home cooking. We ate here twice and all our food choices were fresh, delicious and like we would fix at home. Yum.
Improve this in GPT way: During our RV trip, we paused in Granite City and discovered this charming cafe. The welcoming staff and home-style cooking made it a true find. We dined here twice—every dish was fresh, delicious, and just like homemade. A real gem!

input: After 3 weeks of working in the area I finally found a place off of Magazine that is not overrated. Friendly staff! Y'all know I love Phò so it's pretty damn good!

input: Our family returned for breakfast again this weekend and the food and service was again impeccable ... Highly recommend
Improve this in GPT way: We returned for breakfast this weekend—once again, the food and service were impeccable. Highly recommended.

input: The kayaking tour at the Santa Cruz Island was great.  My husband and I had a wonderful time.  Jen, our tour guide, was helpful and informative.  We had a lot of fun exploring the caves.  We didn't expect much but this tour definitely exceeded our expectation.
Improve this in GPT way: Our Santa Cruz Island kayaking tour was fantastic. Jen, our guide, was both knowledgeable and helpful, making our cave exploration a delight. It far exceeded our modest expectations, providing a wonderful experience for my husband and me.

input: Definitely recommend for anyone looking for a delicious meal at a reasonable price. The shrimp and goat cheese crepes are a must have!
Improve this in GPT way: Highly recommended for a delicious, affordable meal. Their shrimp and goat cheese crepes are an absolute must-try.

input:
After living in the STL area for way over 10 years now, I am both ashamed and remorseful to admit that I ate here for the FIRST time just a few weeks ago. I am ashamed because it's a St. Louis tradition and remorseful because I missed out on it for so..many...years! 

This place is amazing. What is not to love! It's a factory where you can get a tour (Friday-Sunday, noon-5pm on the hour), there's a shop, bar, and dining area. They also host many event with live music on the weekends. It's fun to just kind of wander and look around - don't worry, you'll get a chance because there will likely be a wait before you dine. The beer is, of course, amazing. The Hefeweizen is my personal favorite and a great start for anyone who is not a huge beer drinker (like myself). Additionally, the food is homegrown and damn good. I had the pizza (recommendation from my server) and it was really spectacular, though I'm admittedly a pizza connoisseur so I enjoy a good pizza pie more than most probably ;P My date had a bison burger which was also really good. 

More fun info: the service is great! I think they tend to hire more funky and alternative people (like tattoo parlor staff) which I support. The quality is what makes this place stand out along with the emphasis on local food and brewery. 

It is a little on the pricier side but for all the experience you get and the quality, it is worth it. I will go again and again and you probably should, too!
Improve this in GPT way:
Having been a resident of the St. Louis area for well over a decade, I confess with a mix of shame and regret that I only experienced this iconic spot for the first time recently. My shame stems from its status as a beloved local tradition, and my regret from all the years I missed out.

This place is truly exceptional. It operates as a functioning factory, offering tours hourly from Friday to Sunday between noon and 5 p.m. Beyond production, the space includes a shop, a bar, and a dining area, frequently hosting weekend events with live music. It’s an engaging environment to explore—and you’ll likely have time to wander, as there’s often a wait for a table.

The beer is, unsurprisingly, superb. My personal favorite is the Hefeweizen, an approachable and excellent choice for those who aren’t avid beer drinkers. The food is outstanding and sourced locally. Upon my server’s recommendation, I tried the pizza, which was spectacular—a high compliment from a self-proclaimed pizza connoisseur. My date’s bison burger was equally impressive.

Adding to the appeal is the excellent service. The staff often brings a vibrant, alternative flair to the experience, which I fully appreciate. The commitment to quality, local sourcing, and craft brewing truly sets this establishment apart.

While it leans toward the pricier side, the overall experience and caliber of offerings justify the cost. I plan to return again and again, and I highly recommend you do the same.

I visited this restaurant 4 times during my 5 days stay. Crazy, right? Here are a list of reasons/pros:

- We were staying a nearby hotel.
- The restaurant opens 11 - 10:30 pretty much every day including new year's day so it fits into our schedule.
- If you are a party of two, chances are you get seated right away.
- $9 per dozen of oysters which is a really great deal by any standard!
- They have a seafood shop next door that sells boiled and fresh seafood to- go.
- Our server (same) is very friendly and recognized us every single time.

Now I want to talk about the reasons why I only give it 3 stars.

- We tried a bunch of stuff which are all pretty mediocre. Raw oysters are not cleaned well. So if your schedule is flexible, go to Superior Seafood during their happy hours for their 50 cents/oyster - better quality and cheaper. Turtle soup has a strange taste so I definitely prefer Felix's. A portion of my boiled shrimps are always mushy somhow, maybe boiled for too long?...
- The ambient is inviting but not comfortable so we basically just finished our food and go. 
- Clean the bathroom!!

Will probably visit again if we stay in the area next time or simply just pick up some seafood quickly.
Improve this in GPT way:
During a recent five-day trip, I found myself dining at this restaurant four times—a testament to its convenience, if not perfection. Its major strengths are practical: proximity to our hotel, reliable hours from 11 AM to 10:30 PM even on holidays, and minimal wait for pairs. The standout value is their oysters at just $9 per dozen. Next door, a seafood shop offers fresh and boiled items to-go, adding to the appeal. Service was consistently warm; our server remembered us each visit.

However, the food was largely mediocre, limiting my rating to three stars. The raw oysters were not thoroughly cleaned. For better quality and price, Superior Seafood’s happy-hour oysters at 50 cents each are superior. The turtle soup had an odd flavor—I prefer Felix’s. Some boiled shrimp were unpleasantly mushy, likely overcooked. While the atmosphere is inviting, it isn’t comfortable for lingering; we ate and left promptly. Additionally, the restrooms need attention.

I would return for the convenience and value, especially for a quick takeaway, but primarily when other options aren’t available.

My experience at TDS was, in a word, *meh*. The atmosphere felt cold and impersonal—not in temperature, but in spirit. The space lacked decor and menu boards, featuring stainless steel prep tables as dining furniture. While staff were plentiful, none wore uniforms or nametags, creating a strangely anonymous feel.

The reasonably priced food was largely good, which makes the major frustration even more glaring: they charge for extra salsa. Improve this in GPT way:

We arrived promptly at 8 a.m. on the new date, only to find the workshop closed and unattended. A call to Michael revealed he was "busy," with a promise to call back. After waiting in our car for thirty minutes with no response, we left for breakfast. We returned at 9:30 a.m., hoping for a resolution.

input: We stayed at The Saint last year for a girl's trip. The lobby is lovely, they have a cool bar and restaurant that you can't help but to "ohh and ahh" over when you walk in.  All the things I'm accustomed too when I stay at a hotel anywhere...ambiance, a little sexy but not overkill! Everyone is so friendly, etc.  I'm thinking "oh shhhh this is going to be a great weekend!"  I checked in a few hours before my girl arrived because I had a ton of work i needed to do. So I set up my laptop ordered some room service and worked for about 4 hours straight. Left out to buy a bottle and get a mani/pedi.  My girl arrives...its about to be some trouble in NOLA... the two of us and no supervision...we pop out for dinner, come back in giggling as usual and we see it...a HUGH flying roach.  I'm freaked out.  I literally walk right out of the room down to the front desk.  I CANNOT!!!! They tell me they're sending a maintenance worker to handle it.  NOT GOOD ENOUGH! If there's one that's bold enough to show itself, he has other cohorts that prefer to live behind the scenes. They give us another room but tell me they can't do more until 8am.  No the room the move us too also has small spiders and other dead small bugs in the corners of the window. The TV doesn't work and one of the lamps doesn't have bulbs in it! COME ON!  At this point its about 3am and I know I'm not staying here past 8:15am. I dont want to sit my purse let alone my luggage in this hotel! I go online to my normal go to hotel, The W and book us there for the rest of the trip! 8am comes and goes no manager comes to our room. I go down and demand to see someone immediately.  This younger gentlemen comes out and apologizes.  I thank him for his apology and politely request ALL of my money back immediately.   He obliged and asked if  I would consider coming back after changes have been made! Bless his heart. NO dear!
Improve this in GPT way:
Our stay at The Saint last year began with all the promise of a perfect girls’ weekend in New Orleans. The lobby was lovely, and the bar and restaurant had that instantly appealing ambiance—stylish and subtly sexy, just right. The staff were uniformly friendly. Settling in early to tackle some work, I thought, “This is going to be great.” I worked from my room for hours, then headed out for a few errands before my friend arrived.

The trouble began that evening. After a fun dinner, we returned to our room giggling—only to be met by a huge flying roach. Horrified, I went straight to the front desk. They offered to send maintenance, but that wasn’t enough for me; where there’s one bold roach, there are likely more hidden away. They relocated us to another room, but said further resolution would have to wait until 8 a.m.

The second room was no better. Small spiders and dead bugs dotted the window corners, the TV was broken, and a lamp lacked bulbs. By 3 a.m., I knew we wouldn’t stay past morning. I didn’t even want to set my purse down. I promptly booked us into The W, my reliable standby, for the remainder of the trip.

8 a.m. came with no manager in sight. I went downstairs and insisted on speaking to someone immediately. A young gentleman appeared, apologized sincerely, and I thanked him—then politely requested a full refund. He complied and asked if we might consider returning after improvements. Bless his heart, but the answer was a firm and final no.

input:
Milktooth is the place to go if you want a good breakfast cocktail and a twist on traditional brunch. At first glance of the menu, you may think you've never heard of any of these foods for breakfast, and you may be right. I guarantee no matter what you order, you're going to enjoy it. 

Milktooth is one of the most popular brunch places in Indy, which means you will typically have a wait. Trust me, it's worth the usual 30 minute wait (on weekends). To make it go by a little faster, they've got a walk up bar for their coffee drinks and pastries. Snack on one of those to give you a preview of the amazing meal you're about to have.

Their menu changes from time to time but they have a few things that stay one the menu but change ingredients. I love all of their variations on a Dutch pancake, and their raclette grilled cheese is to die for.  If you're making this a boozy breakfast, don't pass up on the michelada. And sit outside if it's warm enough!
Improve this in GPT way:
For a standout brunch that redefines the morning meal, Milktooth is your destination. The menu immediately intrigues, featuring inventive dishes you likely haven’t encountered at breakfast—and each one is a guaranteed delight. As one of Indianapolis’ most sought-after spots, a wait is typical, especially on weekends. Consider it time well spent; the 30-minute delay is a small price for the experience. To ease the anticipation, visit the walk-up bar for a expertly crafted coffee or a pastry, offering a preview of the culinary excellence to come.

While the seasonal menu rotates, certain staples remain, creatively reinterpreted. The Dutch pancake, in all its variations, is a must, and the raclette grilled cheese is utterly sublime. For those indulging in a boozy brunch, the michelada is an essential choice. When weather permits, secure a patio seat to complete the perfect outing.

input:
Oh Chickie's and Pete's, you are the perfect place to watch some sports and indulge. 

No doubt this is not the best food I've ever had but, if you can get a seat, grab some beer with mussels red and crab fries, there's no way not to thoroughly enjoy this place during a game or any time you're down by the stadiums. 

My favs are the crab fries, mussels red (white is overloaded with garlic that I can't always take it), the spicy pull and peel shrimp, steamers, and if the mood is right the blue crabs (it's a lot of work but tasty). This place also makes getting down and dirty with your food easy. There are sinks all over so you can rinse the mess off your hands once you're done....good touch.

To sum it up, Chickie's and Pete's is a Philadelphia institution and always a good time. I strongly suggest going at least once to enjoy the experience. 

Please note: Make sure to remember two things before coming during major sporting events. 1. You'll never get a table and 2. You'll deal with a ton of drunk people. I've absolutely been one of these people before and we can get annoying unless you're in the right frame of mind. :)
Improve this in GPT way:
Chickie’s and Pete’s is the quintessential spot for catching a game and treating yourself. While the food may not be the absolute best you’ll ever have, securing a seat with a beer, an order of mussels red, and their famous crab fries guarantees a thoroughly enjoyable time—whether during a matchup or any visit near the stadiums.

My personal favorites include the crab fries, mussels red (I find the white version overly garlicky), the spicy pull-and-peel shrimp, steamers, and, when I’m up for the effort, the delightfully messy blue crabs. The restaurant makes diving into messy fare easy, with sinks conveniently placed throughout to wash up afterward—a thoughtful touch.

In short, Chickie’s and Pete’s is a Philadelphia institution and always promises a good time. I highly recommend visiting at least once for the full experience.

A quick heads-up for major sporting events: expect two things. First, you likely won’t find a table. Second, you’ll encounter plenty of enthusiastic, drink-fueled fans. Having been one myself, I can say the atmosphere is fun—but only if you’re in the right mindset for it.

input: I cannot even believe someone gave this place one star. Here's the scoop. They have the BEST cannoli in the city. Termini's are no where NEAR as good, and Isgro's is far too hyped up for the quality. Potito's is my go to for cannoli, i wouldn't even THINK about going anywhere else. I'm there every xmas eve, and will be for the rest of my days. I stood in line for isgros for TWO HOURS this year for a tirimisu, i walked right into potito's and picked up my bambino cannoli stuffed cannoli. it's as good as it sounds, trust me.
Improve this in GPT way: It’s hard to believe anyone would rate this place just one star. Let me be clear: they serve the best cannoli in the city. Termini’s doesn’t come close, and Isgro’s is overrated. Potito’s is my absolute go-to—I wouldn’t consider anywhere else. Every Christmas Eve, without fail, I’m there. This year, I waited two hours at Isgro’s for tiramisu, but at Potito’s, I walked right in and picked up my perfectly stuffed bambino cannoli. It’s every bit as incredible as it sounds—trust me.

input: Truly, I cannot say enough good things about this tiny, authentic, perfectly delicious eatery!  Growing up in the panhandle of Texas, we had plenty of authentic Mexican food in our home, and I'm always searching for good Mexican restaurants. El Limon is the best I've ever had in the state of Pennsylvania!  Sopes, tostadas, enchiladas, fajitas, burritos, fish tacos....all excellent and sooooo reasonable!  Waitstaff is always pleasant and attentive.  Best two features: homemade tamales and free margaritas!!  Bring the entire family for an amazing Mexican feast!  Ole!
Improve this in GPT way: I cannot praise this small, authentic eatery enough! As someone raised on Texan Mexican cuisine, I’m always seeking great Mexican food. El Limon is the best I’ve found in Pennsylvania. Their sopes, enchiladas, fajitas, and fish tacos are all excellent and reasonably priced. The staff is pleasant and attentive. Highlights include homemade tamales and complimentary margaritas. Bring the whole family for a fantastic feast—Olé!

input:
I'm giving this joint 4 stars because they have earned it, but they are definitely 5 star material, if they work out a few kinks. Granted, they just opened, so some of the errors I've experienced (I work in the area, so I've been there several times) will probably get worked out and they are more than willing to make corrections and accommodations when they mess up. 

But over all, the food is REALLY good. Unlike my fellow Yelp-ers, I would say that ther pizza is not their strong suit - its kinds greasy and not sure if they use 100% mozzarella - tastes like its cut with something cheaper. However, so far I've had:  

The Quaker (Chicken version) - Delicious. They make their chicken steaks with the chunky chicken, which I like much more than the shredded version. They could season the chicken more, but the cheese was melted perfectly and the veggies were fresh. 

The fries - crisp and flavorful. I didn't even need ketchup, and I always eat ketchup on my fries

The onion rings - a little greasy, but very tasty and crisp. The onions stayed in the breading and didn't slide out when you bit them (which I hate). 

Spanakopita - mine was a little over cooked, but the flavors were really good

Baklava - VERY GOOD! 

Signature Salad - The veggies they use are very fresh which will make or break a salad. Their balsamic is great too!

The (turkey) Greek Burger - one of the best turkey burgers I've ever had! The patty was moist and flavorful all on its own, but then they top it with what must be homemade tzatziki. I could eat a bowl of that stuff! My burger had romaine instead of the advertised arugula, but it was very fresh, so I didn't mind as much. I also asked for feta, which I didn't get, but that sauce made me forget all about it. 

Overall, this place is great! Provided they don't stray from the high quality standard they are setting, I will keep going back.
Improve this in GPT way:
I’m awarding this spot four stars—a rating they’ve certainly earned—though they absolutely have the potential to reach five. As a new establishment, there are still a few kinks to iron out, but given their recent opening, I expect these will improve with time. I work nearby and have visited several times already, and I appreciate that the staff is consistently willing to correct any mistakes.

Overall, the food is genuinely excellent. Contrary to some other reviews, I’d say the pizza isn’t their strongest offering—it tends to be somewhat greasy, and the cheese doesn’t taste like pure mozzarella. However, nearly everything else I’ve tried has been impressive:

- **The Quaker (chicken version):** Delicious. The chicken is satisfyingly chunky rather than shredded, though it could use more seasoning. The cheese was perfectly melted and the vegetables fresh.
- **The fries:** Crisp and full of flavor—so good I didn’t even reach for ketchup.
- **Onion rings:** A touch greasy but crispy and tasty, with the onion staying firmly inside the breading.
- **Spanakopita:** Slightly overcooked on my visit, but the flavors were wonderful.
- **Baklava:** Exceptionally good.
- **Signature Salad:** Made with very fresh vegetables and a excellent balsamic dressing.
- **Greek Burger (turkey):** One of the best turkey burgers I’ve had—moist, flavorful, and topped with what tastes like homemade tzatziki sauce. I did receive romaine instead of arugula and missed the feta I’d asked for, but the tzatziki was so good it hardly mattered.

In all, this is a great place. If they maintain the high standards they’re setting now, I’ll definitely be back.

input:
A truly delightful find! This is the transformed Carrow's Restaurant on Plumb and Kietzke that was saved by the wrecking ball by its beautiful redwood beams and fascia. The food was fantastic. My wife had the tri-tip salad -- greens on one side of the plate with a balsamic vinagrette balanced by four good-sized slices of medium-rare tri-tip and potato "croutons" --
little heavenly bits of crunchy potatoes. I had the tri/tip/chicken combo, selecting the fresh corn salad and potato salad as my two sides. It was so good that we ordered dessert as well (not something I do regularly). The offering was lemon meringue, mudd pie, apple pie, and ice cream. We shared the first -- again delicious, with real, perfectly set and browned meringue. The prices were very reasonable for the quality of food and the experience. We've already recommended to family and friends locally, and expect to return soon. Well done!
Improve this in GPT way: A truly delightful find! This transformed Carrow’s Restaurant on Plumb and Kietzke was saved from demolition by its beautiful redwood beams and fascia. The food was fantastic. My wife enjoyed a tri-tip salad—fresh greens with balsamic vinaigrette, balanced by four generous slices of medium-rare tri-tip and heavenly, crunchy potato “croutons.” I chose the tri-tip and chicken combo, with fresh corn salad and potato salad as sides—so satisfying we indulged in dessert, which I rarely do. Options included lemon meringue, mud pie, apple pie, and ice cream. We shared the lemon meringue, featuring perfectly set, browned meringue. Prices were very reasonable for the quality and experience. Already recommended locally, we plan to return soon. Well done!

Improve this in GPT way: I recently had my car tinted at Orange Tint and Tune and received fantastic service. Their complimentary pick-up within four miles was extremely convenient. input: Stayed here three nights on business.  The property is located very close to the airport but you really don't hear it.  The rooms are standard TownePlace Suite rooms with a refrigerator, stove, etc..  The area in which the hotel is located is quiet with a combination of other hotels and office buildings.  It's about a 20 minute drive to the downtown or university area.  About 5-10 minutes from Pima Air Museum.  There are not too many restaurants close by but there are some fast food options and a sandwich place called Baggins that was really good and within walking distance.  The staff of the hotel was really friendly and helpful.  The breakfast is standard continental with a couple of hot options. They also have a reception on weekday evenings.  My only complaint is that the food and drink go quickly so get there early.  You could use this as a dinner if you wanted.  I got there about 45 minutes after it started and although there was food left there were very few soft drinks left (no diet).  They could improve by keeping the area stocked throughout the period.  Anyway, the rooms are nice, beds are comfortable and area is safe.
Improve this in GPT way:
I stayed at this TownePlace Suites for three nights on a business trip. Its location is extremely convenient to the airport, yet aircraft noise was never an issue. The room was the brand's standard layout, well-equipped with a refrigerator, stove, and other essentials. The surrounding neighborhood is quiet, composed mainly of other hotels and office parks. Downtown and the university area are roughly a 20-minute drive away, while the Pima Air & Space Museum is only 5-10 minutes by car.

Dining options in the immediate vicinity are limited, though there are a few fast-food outlets and an excellent walkable sandwich shop called Baggins. The hotel staff were consistently friendly and helpful. The complimentary breakfast offered the usual continental spread plus a few hot items, and they host a reception on weekday evenings. My sole suggestion would be for better replenishment of the evening food and drinks; by my arrival 45 minutes in, soft drinks (especially diet) were nearly gone. Despite this, the rooms are pleasant, the beds comfortable, and the area feels very safe. It’s a solid and reliable choice for a business stay.

input:
We got diverted to Tampa and decided to make the drive to Orlando but first we needed somewhere to eat. Wanting to avoid chain restaurants, yelp steered us towards this little local gem!

The ladies had the 7 oz. Tampa strip and the gents both had a 14 oz. ribeye. They grill their steaks over oak and citrus Wood and the smoky flavor is to die for! We are big fans of our smoker back home and cook our steaks this way as well, it's rare to find steak cooked over woodsmoke in most places and this was worth the side trip!  Sides were veggies and sweet potatoes. The wines on offer were so reasonably priced- most under $20 a bottle but a decent selection. They just don't mark them up 5x like most places! 

Our waitress Lisa also made great recommendations and her service was welcoming, friendly, and excellent. We are so glad we went local instead of to a chain. Bookmarking this place for a return trip next time I am in Tampa for sure!
Improve this in GPT way:
After an unexpected diversion to Tampa, we chose to drive to Orlando—but first, we needed a meal. Eager to skip chain restaurants, we followed Yelp to this local gem.

My wife and her friend ordered the 7 oz. Tampa strip, while my friend and I chose the 14 oz. ribeye. Each steak is grilled over oak and citrus wood, delivering a smoky, unforgettable flavor. As avid home smokers, we rarely find steaks cooked over real woodfire elsewhere—this alone made the detour worthwhile. Our sides included fresh vegetables and sweet potatoes. The wine list was another delight, with most bottles under $20 and thoughtfully chosen, not marked up excessively.

Our waitress, Lisa, provided warm, friendly service and spot-on recommendations. Choosing local over a chain was the best decision. I’ve already bookmarked this spot for my next visit to Tampa.

input: The owner of this location (and two others including Southampton) reached out to me after my previous review. Improve this in GPT way: After my earlier review, the owner of this location (and two others) contacted me. input: By far the best deli I have ever been to in the US. YEP, the US. Lots of crazy choices and oh it is hard to pick!! The Muffalata is so big 4 people can share. It is so tasty and amazing! input: Came here after my husband bought home their lemon pepper wings. They have plenty of flavors. Improve this in GPT way:
My husband introduced me to their fantastic lemon pepper wings, and I was impressed by the extensive flavor selection. It spans familiar options like mild to unique New Orleans-inspired tastes such as yaka mein and noonie bird. Their drinks are exceptional—the watermelon one is absolutely divine. While the area isn’t the most ideal, they’re positively contributing to the community. Located near a daiquiri shop, it feels fine during daylight hours, though I’d avoid visiting alone at night. Overall, it’s definitely worth a visit—you might even spot Skip there!

(Word count: 109)

input:
Back to Tom Jones and time to update my review. I didn't see that odd ATM type machine that only lets you withdraw money to apply to your check. It's no longer there-used to be next to restrooms. There is still a payphone back there which I love. There are now ATM's at front entrance.
  The blue ribbon is now $3.79, but still a bargain since it includes everything: pancakes, 2 eggs, toast, sausage, bacon,juice & coffee. I ate here with my kids. My daughter's choice. Says she "loves Tom Jones". Our meals included blue ribbons, french toast, chicken, club sandwich & baked potato . Everyone gets what they like. 
   I don't smell stale smoke and would not call it dirty.  I like the "loud" orange booths. I feel like I went back in time with these and the payphone. Service is always fast and I always seem to get a different waitress. Don't know where they find these young ladies but they're good. I've seen different managers there and they are all quick and on top of things-which makes a good manager.
   Since it's my daughter's fave I'm bumping it up from 4 to 5 stars.
Improve this in GPT way:
Returning to Tom Jones, it’s time to refresh my review. I noticed the unusual ATM that only allowed withdrawals to pay your check is gone—it used to be near the restrooms. A classic payphone remains in that spot, which I adore. Now, standard ATMs are available at the front entrance.

The Blue Ribbon breakfast is now $3.79, still a steal because it includes everything: pancakes, two eggs, toast, sausage, bacon, juice, and coffee. I dined here with my kids at my daughter’s request—she declares she “loves Tom Jones.” Our meals featured the Blue Ribbon, French toast, chicken, a club sandwich, and a baked potato. There’s truly something for everyone.

The place doesn’t smell of stale smoke, nor would I call it dirty. I enjoy the vibrant orange booths; along with the payphone, they transport me back in time. Service is consistently quick, and I’m always served by a different, capable waitress—I’m not sure where they find these impressive young women. I’ve also observed various managers, each attentive and efficiently overseeing operations, which defines good management.

Because it’s my daughter’s favorite, I’m raising my rating from four to five stars.

Improve this in GPT way: As an amateur athlete and single mother, I first encountered Dr. Ferrel during a softball game where I suffered a severe injury. input:
I've been wanting to try Trust Me BBQ for over a year now.  I stopped in there about 3 months ago and waited in line for 10 minutes with no service and left.  After reading reviews, I figured I'd give it a chance again just to see what all the fuss is about.  The food was 50/50 but the service was horrible so I'll likely never return.  The gentleman behind the counter didn't speak, smile or engage with us at all, I felt like I was at a vending machine.  Once we finally ordered, he didn't even listen to the order and put the wrong sides in our meals, we had to correct him while he was serving.  All in all, I will just stick with Down to the Bone BBQ

Pros:  BBQ Sauce is delicious, macaroni salad was different and interesting, "pulled" pork was moist.

Cons:  Chicken was more dry than a sheet of paper, inedible even with the BBQ Sauce.  Mac & Cheese was served from a pan that has probably been on the steam table for 2-3 days.  Collard Greens were very mildly flavored.
Improve this in GPT way:
For over a year, I’d been eager to try Trust Me BBQ. A previous attempt three months ago ended when I left after waiting ten minutes without service. Recently, motivated by reviews, I decided to give it another chance. Unfortunately, while the food was a mixed bag, the service confirmed my worst impressions and likely ensures I won’t return.

The counter attendant offered no greeting, smile, or engagement, making the interaction feel transactional. After we ordered, he didn’t listen carefully, resulting in incorrect sides that we had to correct on the spot. The positives included a delicious BBQ sauce, an interesting macaroni salad, and moist pulled pork. However, the chicken was unpleasantly dry, the mac and cheese tasted days old, and the collard greens were bland. Overall, I’ll be sticking with Down to the Bone BBQ for future cravings.

input: Was in town for a week and came by this little hole in the wall.  The pa nang chicken was excellent.  I ordered one star spicy and it came quick.  Will definitely return.

A high five for the on the rocks margaritas and house made white or red sangria - definitely worth the trip!
Improve this in GPT way:
Cinco de Mayo here means expertly crafted margaritas with rock salt, house-made sangria, and delicious fried fare. While not a strictly Mexican restaurant, this spot excels by fusing diverse ethnic flavors into uniquely inventive recipes. They pour tequila with skill and have even opened a nearby wine bar for overflow and special bottles. A high five is due for their outstanding on-the-rocks margaritas and sangria—making the visit undoubtedly worthwhile.

input:
This small little donut bakery is located in one of Hermitage's oldest shopping centers! 

I can imagine baking donuts is a hard job, let alone running the business...it's one of those jobs that starts in the wee hours of the morning so that the donuts are freshly made daily!

Yeu, the owner, serves not only your common popular donuts, but he also serves donuts with bacon on top, apple fritters, pigs in a blanket, breakfast pastries, and  kolaches....in addition to these yummy treats...he makes doughssants....they are what seems to be a scandalous marriage of a donut and a croissant...!!!!!!!! Need I say more? Yeah...you heard me. A doughssant! Worth the trip just to eat one of these! 

Prices are considerably cheap! The doughssants are only $1.99 each! The regular donuts are about $.60 each! 

These sweet donuts are my favorite treats to buy for my kid's school teachers...and they love them! 

Coffee also served here!
Improve this in GPT way:
Tucked into one of Hermitage’s oldest shopping centers, this charming donut shop is a testament to dedication. The craft begins in the early morning hours, ensuring every treat is baked fresh daily.

Owner Yeu offers both classic favorites and inventive creations. Beyond popular donuts, the menu features bacon-topped varieties, apple fritters, pigs in a blanket, breakfast pastries, and kolaches. The true star, however, is the “doughssant”—a delightful and indulgent cross between a donut and a croissant. It’s an experience worth the trip alone.

With remarkably affordable prices—doughssants at just $1.99 and regular donuts around $0.60—it’s a perfect spot for a sweet gesture. I often bring these treats for my children’s teachers, who always adore them. Pair your selection with a cup of their served coffee for the complete visit.

input: Hands down the worst chicken and rice plate I've ever had. When I ordered I was told there was no sauce on the chicken (as I wanted, healthy). Improve this in GPT way:
This is, without question, the most disappointing chicken and rice dish I’ve encountered. I specifically ordered it without sauce for a healthier option and was assured there was none. input: Great experience purchasing a washer and dryer.  I just bought a new home and needed all new appliances. input:
Went here based on the high ratings and raves from people.  The entire experience was underwhelming from start to finish.  Their website which is fairly useless if you want to figure out the menu before going, you have to pick your location choice out of 3 locations and then drill down to the bottom to see the weak descriptions of their menu offering, no explanations and no price, just this

    Roast Beef
    Roast Beef Combo
    Roast Pork
    Roast Pork Combo
    Baked Ham
    Baked Ham Combo
    Roast Turkey
    Roast Turkey Combo
    Broccoli Rabe
    Broccoli Rabe Combo


No explanation of whats in a combo (its just where they add cheese by the way)

The table placecard (instead of menu) had a more detailed description than the website.  

When I walked in, its more bar than restaurant, no big deal, but there were tables.  Since I couldnt decide and the sandwiches werent too expensive at $6.85, I got the roast beef and roast port combos.

I got my two sandwiches fast enough, but the roast beef was cold and the roast pork was hot.  Not sure how a cook (for lack of a better word) could serve 2 things at the same time with such a temperature differential, one was obviously sitting for awhile.  I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I finished the roast pork, and supposedly it was reheated, since it was warmer, but it was still cold-ish compared to my roast pork I had just finished.  The waitress did offer to replace it when she inquired, but I was in a hurry and didnt really care for a hot version of this sandwich.

The sandwiches were very skimpy on meat, but they "made up for it" by adding too much gravy to make it overly messy and the bread was disintegrating.  The menu place card mentions the "wet meat" option where you get less gravy, I strongly recommend you get it that style, especially if the gravy overpower the meat and structural integrity of the sandwich.
Improve this in GPT way:
Based on the numerous positive reviews and high ratings, my expectations were quite high for this establishment. Unfortunately, the entire experience proved underwhelming from start to finish. The initial disappointment began with their website, which is nearly useless for planning a visit. To view the menu, you must first select one of three locations and scroll to the bottom, only to find a sparse, unhelpful list. It offers no descriptions, no prices, and simply reads: Roast Beef, Roast Beef Combo, Roast Pork, Roast Pork Combo, and so on. There is no explanation of what a "combo" entails—which, I later learned, merely means adding cheese.

Upon arrival, I found the ambiance more bar than restaurant, though tables were available. The physical table card provided more detail than the website. Since the sandwiches were reasonably priced at $6.85 and I was indecisive, I ordered both a roast beef and a roast pork combo.

The food arrived quickly, but with a glaring issue: the roast beef was cold while the roast pork was hot. It was perplexing how two sandwiches served simultaneously could have such a drastic temperature difference, suggesting one had been sitting for some time. I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef. While it returned warmer, it remained noticeably cooler than the pork I had just finished. She kindly offered a replacement, but I was pressed for time and had lost my appetite for another version of the sandwich.

Furthermore, the sandwiches were surprisingly skimpy on meat. This was poorly compensated for by an excessive amount of gravy, which made them overly messy and caused the bread to disintegrate. The menu card mentions a "wet meat" option with less gravy; I strongly recommend choosing this style. It would help prevent the gravy from overwhelming both the flavor of the meat and the structural integrity of the sandwich itself.
